pillars.title: Biomedical Lens
pillars.body: Applying engineering principles to real healthcare outcomes and functional human movement.

pillars.title: Mechanical Depth
pillars.body: Exploring mechanisms, kinematics, and structural design through a hands-on innovation challenge.

pillars.title: Real Impact
pillars.body: Designing for a vulnerable population whose daily independence is affected by the existing gap in the market.

pillars.title: Iterative Process
pillars.body: Experiencing the full engineering design loop — from need identification to physical prototype testing.

items.title: Problem Identification
items.body: Observed limitations in existing transfer bench products. Conducted initial literature review on senior falls and bathing ADLs.

items.title: Background Research
items.body: Reviewed clinical literature, existing patents, and assistive technology standards. Identified key functional gaps.

items.title: Stakeholder Interviews
items.body: Conducted 8 structured interviews with mechanical engineers, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, PSWs, and end users.

items.title: Requirements & Ideation
items.body: Defined project requirements. Generated and evaluated multiple design concepts using morph charts and decision matrices.

items.title: CAD Design
items.body: Developed full 3D model in Autodesk Fusion. Iterated on mechanism geometry based on ergonomic constraints and interview feedback.

items.title: Testing, Analysis & Reflection
items.body: Completed FMEA, free body diagram analysis, and material selection. Compiled findings and portfolio documentation.

about_project.description: An engineering investigation into senior bathing mobility, combining mechanical design with assistive healthcare.
about_project.tools: Autodesk Fusion, free-body diagrams, safety factors, FMEA, ergonomic analysis

interviews.heading: Learning from Eight Domain Experts
interviews.intro: To ground the engineering decisions in real-world clinical and professional insight, structured interviews were conducted with eight stakeholders. Their feedback directly shaped the final design.
